units.reason: P-005 (proposal and adoption), P-008 (members), P-047 ('greater or less than the sums presented').

units.sentence: Option C, a proposal to change how drafts are built, was filed on Nov 4.
units.evidence_span: A substitute motion was made by Vice Chair Abdur-Rahman and seconded by Commissioner Thorne, to file.

units.sentence: Filing set Option C aside without approving it.
units.marker: {analysis: its status is "Filed" (P-024), and its history shows no later action (P-025)}
units.reason: P-024 status 'Filed'; P-025 shows no later action.

units.sentence: said that process is
units.problem: Misquote. P-073's words are 'The process we’ve laid out is more transparent and open than anything we’ve had in recent years.' The page's quote ('more transparent and open than any county process in Georgia') is in no passage and turns a comparison with Fulton's own recent past into a statewide claim. The rest is supported: Ellis sponsored the process (P-016) and Option C would change it (P-024). Line 214 quotes him correctly.
units.suggested_fix: ...said that process is "more transparent and open than anything we’ve had in recent years." [P-073, P-016, P-024]

units.sentence: Commissioner Dana Barrett, who opposed Option C, proposed it
units.problem: Wrong side. Barrett sponsored Option C (P-032), moved to approve it (P-025), voted yes on Oct 21 (P-033) and voted no on filing it (P-034). 'Who opposed Option C, proposed it' contradicts itself. The quoted purpose is verbatim from P-024.
units.suggested_fix: Commissioner Dana Barrett, who sponsored Option C, proposed it "to ensure transparency and informed decision-making in the development of the Fulton County budget." [P-024, P-032]

units.sentence: Solicitor-General Keith Gammage, one of nine justice officials seeking more money
units.problem: Wrong count. P-069 and P-076 name six officials (sheriff, district attorney, solicitor-general, court clerk, probate judge, public defender), not nine; the page says six elsewhere (lines 16, 142, 165, 171). The Gammage quote is verbatim from P-077.
units.suggested_fix: Solicitor-General Keith Gammage, one of six justice officials seeking more money, said they believe there is "a lack of proper investment in the entire ecosystem of the courts." [P-077, P-069, P-070]

units.sentence: No archived source argues for Option A over Option B, or the reverse.
units.marker: {editorial: no archived statement argues for adopting the proposal unchanged or for changing it; both options keep today's process}
units.reason: True as far as the passages show. It is a checkable claim about the sources, so {analysis} would be the better tag.

units.sentence: The officials' request for a January vote has no line; our sources quote no one making it.
units.marker: {editorial: P-070 gives the request only in Atlanta News First's words}
units.reason: P-070 gives the request only in Atlanta News First's own words.

units.sentence: Option B is the most balanced choice.
units.problem: The page recommends an option. This breaks the nonpartisan rule (no ratings or endorsements; same treatment for every option), contradicts the sentence before it, and no {editorial} tag can license a recommendation.
units.reason: Invalid: an endorsement, not framing.

framing_issues.text: Option B is the most balanced choice.
framing_issues.issue: The page endorses one option. That breaks the nonpartisan rule (no endorsements; the same template and strongest case for every option) and contradicts the sentence before it, which says no archived source argues for A over B.

framing_issues.text: Your 2027 county property tax will go down
framing_issues.issue: Presents an unknown future outcome as settled, in a section readers see first. It conflicts with line 36 ('not known') and the tag's own evidence, and recasts a limit on requests for extra money as a cap on total spending.

framing_issues.text: "more transparent and open than any county process in Georgia."
framing_issues.issue: Altered quote attributed to a named official in the values guide; it inflates Ellis's comparison with recent Fulton practice into a statewide claim.

framing_issues.text: who opposed Option C, proposed it
framing_issues.issue: The values guide puts Barrett on the wrong side of her own resolution, which misleads readers matching their values to a side.
Wrong accessibility contact number (P-067 gives 404.612.8200); people who need an accommodation would be sent to a wrong number.

framing_issues.text: Bridget Thorne, also on the Budget Commission
framing_issues.issue: Names a third commissioner as a member, contradicting line 64 and P-021; readers may contact or blame the wrong official, and it blurs the core dispute over a two-commissioner panel.

framing_issues.text: by its first regular meeting in January 2027
framing_issues.issue: Wrong adoption deadline (first instead of second regular meeting); contradicts lines 10, 14, 16 and 72, and a reader could think the vote is due Jan 6.

framing_issues.text: A proposal is due by Nov 25
framing_issues.issue: Wrong proposal deadline; contradicts lines 8 and 69 (Nov 15).
Wrong approval date for the members; contradicts line 77 (Aug 19) and mixes up the Aug 5 vote creating the commission with the Aug 19 vote seating its members.
Says the General Fund pays for water and the airport, contradicting line 20 (specialty funds) and P-052; misleads readers about what the property-tax-backed fund covers.
Inflates the coalition from six to nine, making the funding push look larger than the sources show.

framing_issues.text: Fulton County residents and property owners
framing_issues.issue: The 'who it affects' line cites P-103, a 2026 budget-message sentence about residents' needs; the property-owner part is inference and should be labeled as such.
Points to a 'Summary tab' this page does not have; the votes are under 'What happened' in Layer 1.
